# HunterX

> AI-Assisted Vulnerability Discovery, Validation & Proof Engine

HunterX is an open-source (Apache-2.0) Python platform for authorized
cybersecurity testing and research. It plans, orchestrates, executes, validates,
correlates and reports security assessments by integrating open-source security
tools. Its differentiator is that it does not stop at candidate detections: it
investigates, verifies, builds reproducible proof, collects evidence, and
produces report-ready findings.

- Author / maintainer: Ahmed Awad (AKA NullC0d3)
- Repository: https://github.com/nullc0d30/HunterX
- Current version: 7.0.0 (released 2026-08-11)
- License: Apache License 2.0
- Language: Python 3.11+
- Platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows (Docker supported)
- Documentation hub: https://nullc0d30.github.io/HunterX/documentation/
- Product site: https://nullc0d30.github.io/HunterX/

## Core model

HunterX organizes authorized security work as missions. The v7 workflow:

DISCOVER → FINGERPRINT → REASON → HYPOTHESIZE → PROBE → VERIFY → PROVE → POC →
REPLAY → CORRELATE → REPORT

The canonical finding concept:

Vulnerability + Evidence + Reproducibility + Impact + PoC = Validated Finding

Finding lifecycle: DETECTED → SUSPECTED → VALIDATING → VALIDATED → PROVEN →
CONFIRMED → REPORT_READY (with FALSE_POSITIVE and INCONCLUSIVE branches).

## Key capabilities

- Autonomous mission orchestration and adaptive mission planning
- Toolchain intelligence: 92 registered open-source security tools with
  machine-readable contracts, structured execution, parsers/normalizers and
  dependency-aware chaining
- Evidence-driven vulnerability validation with hypothesis testing
- Vulnerability Proof & PoC Validation Engine: proof contracts, minimal safe
  proofs, replay, reproducibility, evidence-driven impact and confidence
- Target intelligence persistence (TIDB): assets, targets, observations,
  findings, evidence, history, relationships
- Cloud & SaaS attack-surface intelligence: AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI, Cloudflare,
  DigitalOcean, Akamai, Fastly, Vercel, Netlify, Heroku, Render, Fly.io,
  Supabase, Firebase, Kubernetes, Docker
- Knowledge graph and cross-tool correlation
- Professional reporting: Markdown, HTML, JSON, SARIF 2.1, PDF, package
- REST API (FastAPI), Docker image, CI/CD integration

## Architecture

Clean Architecture Python core under `src/hunterx`: domain, application,
infrastructure, engines, agents, tools, plugins, knowledge, reporting, config,
CLI and API. Persistence via TIDB (SQL, SQLite default / PostgreSQL supported,
Alembic migrations).

## Tool ecosystem

HunterX integrates with and orchestrates open-source security tools, including
(integration status per tool is documented, never overclaimed):

Recon: Amass, Subfinder, Assetfinder, Findomain, DNSx, MassDNS, Shuffledns,
theHarvester, BBOT, SpiderFoot. Network: Naabu, Nmap, Masscan, RustScan. HTTP:
HTTPx, WhatWeb, Katana, Gospider, Hakrawler, GAU, Waybackurls, URLFinder.
Fuzzing: FFUF, Feroxbuster, Gobuster, Dirsearch. Parameters: Arjun, ParamSpider,
Kiterunner, LinkFinder, SecretFinder, xnLinkFinder. Validation: Nuclei, Dalfox,
XSStrike, SQLmap, Ghauri, Commix, Interactsh, Tplmap, SSTImap, XXEinjector,
GraphQLmap, InQL. Secrets/SAST: Gitleaks, TruffleHog, detect-secrets, Semgrep.
Proxy: OWASP ZAP, mitmproxy. Exploitation: Metasploit, SearchSploit, ExploitDB.
Knowledge: PayloadsAllTheThings, SecLists, FuzzDB. Cloud/container: Prowler,
Trivy, Syft, Grype, OSV-Scanner.

Full list: https://nullc0d30.github.io/HunterX/tool-ecosystem/

## PoC / evidence model

HunterX treats proof as part of vulnerability validation. Proofs are minimal,
safe, structured artifacts (never arbitrary executable scripts). PoCs are
replayed deterministically; reproducibility requires repeated successful
replays. Impact is classified strictly from captured evidence; confidence is a
versioned, weighted policy over named factors. The engine is not a
weaponization engine — data destruction, persistence, reverse shells, DoS and
mass data extraction are never scheduled.

## Responsible use

HunterX is designed for use only against systems you own or are explicitly
authorized to test. You are responsible for obtaining appropriate authorization
before testing any system and for complying with applicable laws and terms of
service. The author is not responsible for misuse. See
https://nullc0d30.github.io/HunterX/responsible-use/
